Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

exceed verb

also go beyond, be more than, surpass, overstep, exceed the limit, top (surpass), outdo

classical

Liv. 39.5: summam octōgintā mīlium (Lewis & Short)
Suet. Tib. 68: statūra quae jūstam excēderet (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 26.19: modum (Lewis & Short)

excēdō, excēdere, excessī, excessum

verb, third conjugation, transitive in this sense

go beyond, exceed (a number, a measure)

Its main sense is “go out, leave”; with an accusative of a number, an age or a measure (modum excēdere) it is “exceed”, from Livy on.

Other words

  • superō, superāre, superāvī, superātum — surpass, be greater than; (intransitive) be more than enough

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 9.32.7: numerō hostis, virtūte Rōmānus superat (Lewis & Short); Cic. Par. 49: cui dēest an cui superat? (Lewis & Short); Traupman 109: superāre, top; Traupman 396

    To be greater than another in something (ablative); also to defeat. Used absolutely, it means “be in excess, be left over”.

  • exsuperō, exsuperāre, exsuperāvī, exsuperātum — rise above, exceed

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. NH 18.168: Nīlus exsuperāvit sēdecim cubita (Lewis & Short)

    Mostly poetic and post-Augustan; of a level or a measure passed (a river over its mark).

Examples

  • Modum nē excesserīs: duo crustula satis sunt.

    Don’t overdo it: two biscuits are enough.composed

See also limit, more, enough.

SourcesLewis & Short: excedo · Lewis & Short: supero · Lewis & Short: exsupero

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 109.
